## Stage 7: who can have their height estimated (`scripts/stage7_height_share.m`, 300 days per case, medium allocation; `results/stage7_height_share.csv`)
The height method (Engyom/DAS- v2.2-sim) needs a walker, parallel to the fibre within 3 m, with at least 8 validated footsteps, detected with SNR >= 12 dB. The along-boundary behaviour (`p_along`, ASSUMED) is the only way to meet it; a crossing person never qualifies (camera instead). The height model itself is NOT called here; the SNR is the engine's local SNR (here always above 26 dB, so the 12 dB condition never binds in simulation: the real value is measured in Phase 0).
| p_along | walking | along-boundary path | height measurable, all intruders | of along-boundary paths | of crossing walkers | of all walkers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 % | 49.7 % | 0.0 % | 0.0 % | n/a | 0.0 % | 0.0 % |
| 10 % | 49.7 % | 4.7 % | 4.1 % | 88.1 % | 0.0 % | 8.3 % |
| 30 % | 49.4 % | 15.2 % | 13.4 % | 87.9 % | 0.0 % | 27.0 % |
Reasons a walker is not measurable (p_along 10 %): crossing 84.5 %, not detected 6.5 %, lane farther than 3 m 0.7 %. Height is a secondary, exploratory indicator (+/- 8 cm); the primary claim is stride, speed and cadence.

| Scenario (drones) | intrusions / 20 days | true alarms: camera / drone / no asset | verified within T_resp (all / Hot) | median verification time | patrol reached (median alarm-to-patrol) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| medium (6) | 453 | 2 / 426 / 0 | 33.9 % / 48.7 % (of 238 Hot) | 536 s | 89.3 % (737 s) |
| high (12) | 509 | 3 / 487 / 0 | 70.6 % / 89.7 % (of 290 Hot) | 220 s | 87.1 % (409 s) |
* The optimization (steady-state availability, cells not alarms) verifies 25 / 61 / 94 % of the Hot CELLS in low / medium / high; the simulation gives 28 / 49 / 90 % of the Hot ALARMS. The medium value is lower because drones are explicit (each busy for the mission and the 27 min charge), so concurrent alarms and false alarms can leave no ready drone, and DAS localization errors move the target. This difference is a result, not a defect.
* Cameras verify only 0.5 to 1 % of the intrusions (they cover 1.9 % of the boundary), as in the optimization report.
* (SUPERSEDED by the update below: the rule changed from 'no alarm' to 'low-priority routing') False alarms per day (any scenario): about 45 (animals about 4, authorized vehicles about 28, background noise about 13), cleared by the verifying asset in about 85 % of the cases. They are dominated by the PLACEHOLDER traffic rate (100 authorized vehicles per site per day) and by the stub's error rate; they load the drones, so they matter for the result. Without the "normal traffic near a road or a checkpoint" rule (`d_road_nonthreat_m` 30 m, `d_site_nonthreat_m` 100 m, both ASSUMED) the first run gave about 340 false alarms per day and starved the drones (low: verified within T_resp 18.8 %).

### Stage 6 update (23 Nov): result, rule change, false alarms, patrol reach (`scripts/stage6_report.m`, 30 days per case, seed 707; stub uniform Pc = 0.983, PLACEHOLDER)
**Result for the optimization chapter.** For medium the simulation verifies 48.7 to 51.5 % of the Hot alarms within T_resp (two runs), against 61 % of the Hot cells in the optimization. The steady-state availability model of the optimization is optimistic: it does not count the time a drone is busy (mission + 27 min charge), nor simultaneous alarms, nor false alarms that also use drones. (low 24-28 % vs 25 %, high 90-93 % vs 94 %: the static model is close when drones are plentiful or very few, and optimistic in between.)

**Rule "vehicle near a road or checkpoint".** It no longer cancels the alert: it is routed with low priority to the site guard and the site's existing cameras (verification at the site, no drone). Radii `d_road_nonthreat_m` = 30 m and `d_site_nonthreat_m` = 100 m (ASSUMED, in the table).
* The zone covers **14.97 km of the 145.46 km boundary = 10.3 %** (12.35 km within 30 m of a paved road, 5.58 km within 100 m of a camera site, overlapping).
* Real intruders that fell inside the zone: 28 of 805 (3.5 %, low), 22 of 839 (2.6 %, medium), 17 of 789 (2.2 %, high); detected: 92.9 %, 100 %, 100 %. Only 4 to 6 of them were classified as a vehicle (and so routed to the site).

**False alarms, medium, authorized vehicles per site per day 50 / 100 / 500 (PLACEHOLDER rate), site guard clears an authorized vehicle with p_site_clear = 0.99 (PLACEHOLDER).** Target FAR_km = 0.01 alarms/km/day = 1.45 per day on 145.46 km.
| Authorized vehicles / site / day | before verification, drone- or camera-cued (per km per day; per day) | before verification, routed to site guards (low priority) | after verification, reaching a patrol (per km per day; per day) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 50 | 0.21 (30.8) | 8.9 (1,292) | 0.109 (15.8) |
| 100 | 0.32 (46.1) | 17.6 (2,553) | 0.212 (30.8) |
| 500 | 1.12 (163) | 87.9 (12,784) | 1.04 (150.8) |
Sensitivity to the site clearing probability (medium, 100 vehicles / site / day): p_site_clear 0.9 -> 1.77 per km per day (257 per day); 0.99 -> 0.212 (30.8); 0.999 -> 0.0525 (7.6).
* **The target 0.01 is not reached in any case; the best case is 0.05, five times the target.** The false alarms that reach a patrol come from two places: authorized vehicles that the site guard fails to clear, and the drone or camera that confirms a false alarm (Pc_drone 0.89, Pc_CCTV 0.85, a quarter of them wrong). Even with perfect site clearing the drone-cued part alone is about 0.03 per km per day.
* **Honest reading:** the classifier stub is the uniform one (errors spread equally over the other classes, Pc 0.983), which is probably pessimistic, because real errors concentrate on a few confusions; the numbers will change when the Brno confusion matrix is used (`config/ai_config.json`, mode `confusion_counts`). The authorized-vehicle rate and p_site_clear are PLACEHOLDERS and drive the result. The first version, which used Pc_CCTV = 0.85 to clear authorized vehicles at guarded sites, gave about 355 false patrol dispatches per day: not credible, which is why p_site_clear is separate.

**Why patrol reach in high (87.0 %) is not above medium (87.4 %).** The patrol is dispatched only after a confirmed verification, so reach equals the share of true alarms confirmed by the asset (Pc_drone 0.89, camera 0.85 -> about 87 to 89 %) times about 100 % (a patrol was free in every case); more drones in high do not raise that ceiling, only the speed. The earlier 89.3 % (medium) against 87.1 % (high) was sampling noise: the 95 % intervals are 84.9 to 89.5 % and 84.4 to 89.2 %. Low is lower (67.4 %) because 164 of 769 true alarms found no ready drone.

## Re-identification (DAS <-> camera), SIMULATED, base drone camera 2.5 m (`report/reid_summary.md`)
With the base drone camera (2.5 m position error, ASSUMED / proxy), people 10 m apart and nobody walking in a pair, **99.6 % [99.5, 99.7] of the person-level links that are made are correct, 79.7 % of the tracks get such a link, 0.3 wrong links per 100 tracks**; with half of the people walking in pairs: 96.6 % [96.2, 97.0] correct, 51.5 % of the tracks linked, 1.7 wrong links per 100. At 2 m spacing the links made are 97.5 % correct (no pairs) and 94.5 % (50 % pairs): **the 0.97 target of the development scenes is not kept in the hard cells** (point value below 0.97 in 98 of 216 base-drone cells). One threshold setting (gate 4 sigma, margin 2) for the whole grid and all camera types. Height adds 1 to 7 points, cadence 6 to 25 points IF the camera can measure it (ASSUMED). Fixed cameras cover only 1.9 % of the boundary.

## Stage 6: dual verification before a patrol is sent (`scripts/stage6_dual.m`, `results/stage6_dual.csv`; 20 days per case, seed 707, 100 authorized vehicles per site per day and p_site_clear 0.99 (PLACEHOLDERS), temporary uniform classifier stub)
Option A = one check (base). Option B = dual everywhere (a drone after a camera, or a second drone after a first one, flying in parallel; a patrol only if BOTH confirm). Option C = dual in Neutral and Cold zones, single in Hot. Site-routed alerts (guard) keep their single check in all options. "Late" = verification later than T_resp (300 s); "not verified" = real intruders without a verification within T_resp (including those the DAS missed or the classifier did not send as an alarm).
| Scenario | Option | False patrols (per km per day) | Median verification time | Median alarm-to-patrol | True alarms verified later than T_resp | Patrol reached (true alarms) | Intruders not verified within T_resp (all / Hot) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| low (3 drones) | A single | 0.217 | 970 s | 1,487 s | 75.2 % | 64.8 % | 81.7 % (22.1 per day) / 78.1 % |
| low | B dual everywhere | 0.189 | 1,294 s | 1,852 s | 84.0 % | 38.2 % | 93.0 % (27.1 per day) / 92.0 % |
| low | C dual Neutral+Cold | 0.191 | 1,194 s | 1,657 s | 77.3 % | 38.5 % | 90.2 % (25.4 per day) / 87.2 % |
| medium (6) | A single | 0.200 | 518 s | 734 s | 61.9 % | 87.5 % | 63.2 % (18.0 per day) / 51.0 % |
| medium | B dual everywhere | 0.199 | 1,193 s | 1,384 s | 78.7 % | 59.6 % | 84.7 % (22.4 per day) / 79.8 % |
| medium | C dual Neutral+Cold | 0.183 | 943 s | 1,061 s | 73.7 % | 70.7 % | 79.0 % (18.9 per day) / 70.7 % |
| high (12) | A single | 0.210 | 225 s | 407 s | 26.7 % | 88.2 % | 29.4 % (7.8 per day) / 8.7 % |
| high | B dual everywhere | 0.188 | 445 s | 591 s | 56.3 % | 80.3 % | 59.2 % (15.3 per day) / 50.6 % |
| high | C dual Neutral+Cold | 0.194 | 234 s | 424 s | 38.1 % | 85.4 % | 41.6 % (10.1 per day) / 21.2 % |
* **Dual verification does NOT bring the false patrols near the target.** It lowers them by 0 to 13 % (0.217 -> 0.189 in low, 0.200 -> 0.199 in medium, 0.210 -> 0.188 in high) while it doubles the median verification time in medium (518 -> 1,193 s) and low, makes far more intruders escape verification within T_resp (medium: 63 % -> 85 %; high: 29 % -> 59 %) and lowers the share of true alarms that reach a patrol (medium 87.5 % -> 59.6 %). The reason is that a second drone is a second mission: drones are busy for the mission and the 27 min charge, so a second check consumes the scarce drones and starves the next alarm.
* The false patrols are dominated by the site-routed alerts (about 25 of about 30 per day: authorized vehicles that the guard fails to clear with p_site_clear = 0.99 PLACEHOLDER), which dual verification does not touch. The part that comes from drone / camera verification errors is about 0.03 to 0.04 per km per day (0.036 measured with the single check, medium): **the target FAR_km = 0.01 is not reachable with the present assets, because the verification errors of the drone and the camera alone (Pc 0.89 and 0.85) already give about 0.03 false alarms per km per day that reach a patrol.**
* Option C (dual only in Neutral and Cold) is the cheaper compromise: in medium it costs 18.9 against 18.0 intruders per day not verified in time (single) and gives the lowest false-patrol rate of the three (0.183), but patrol reach falls from 87.5 % to 70.7 %; in high it adds 2 intruders per day. It does not fix the main source of false patrols.

## The false-alarm result is governed by one PLACEHOLDER: p_site_clear (`scripts/stage6_report.m`, medium, 100 authorized vehicles per site per day, 30 days)
About 25 of the roughly 30 false patrols per day are authorized vehicles at checkpoints and interdiction points that the site guard fails to clear, so the false-patrol rate follows the PLACEHOLDER `p_site_clear` (probability that the guard clears an authorized vehicle) almost one to one. The headline "FAR_km = 0.01 is not reachable with the present assets" holds at every value tried; what changes is by how much:
| p_site_clear (PLACEHOLDER) | false patrols reaching a patrol, per km per day | per day | against the target 0.01 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.90 | 1.770 | 257 | 177 times |
| **0.99 (base)** | **0.212** | 30.8 | 21 times |
| 0.999 | 0.0525 | 7.6 | 5 times |
Even with a perfect guard the drone / camera verification errors alone leave about 0.03 to 0.04 per km per day (Pc 0.89 and 0.85); with the authorized-vehicle rate at 50 / 100 / 500 per site per day and p_site_clear 0.99 the value is 0.109 / 0.212 / 1.04. No value of p_site_clear is measured: it needs real guard data (Phase 0).

## Stage 9: full Monte Carlo (SIMULATED; `report/stage9_results.md`, `results/stage9/`)
394 simulated days per case, 10,004 real intruder events per case (common random numbers: the same intruders and non-intrusion events in every case). Base classifier stub Pc 0.983 (ASSUMED); Brno matrix and groups are SENSITIVITIES.

**Design result: the DAS misses cluster at the far ends of the channels, and a large share is in Hot cells.** With the medium allocation, 416 of 10,004 intruders (4.2 %) are missed by the DAS: **0 % within 10 km of an interrogator, 6.4 % at 10 to 15 km and 12.2 % at 15 to 20 km** (the missed ones are on average 15.4 km from their interrogator, the detected ones 8.8 km), because the signal falls with the round-trip loss while the receiver noise is fixed. 65 % of the misses are in Hot cells (60 % of the intruders are in Hot cells; the miss rate is 4.5 % in Hot, 3.2 % in Neutral, 6.7 % in Cold), and ten cells hold 60 % of all misses; walking is the weakest signal (6.8 % missed against 0 % for running and digging). **Why it is a design matter:** the optimization puts the 4 interrogators where the cost is the same, with no term for the distance; 53 % of the Hot boundary is more than 10 km from an interrogator (24 % more than 15 km), against 35 % (17 %) for Neutral and 51 % (13 %) for Cold. The three scenarios place the interrogators differently at the same cost (arc positions 27 / 65 / 102 / 138 km in low, 23 / 60 / 93 / 131 km in medium, 1 / 34 / 73 / 111 km in high), so a tie-break that minimizes the distance of Hot cells to their interrogator (or a Pd-aware second stage) would lower the missed share at no extra cost. A shorter channel (a fifth interrogator) is not needed to get this; it is an unused degree of freedom of the allocation.

**Why Pd here (95.8 to 96.4 %) differs from 0.969 (optimization) and 0.977 (window library).** 0.969 is a literature value for one disturbance site (`zeng2024`). 0.977 is the average of the window library over five distances (0.5, 5, 10, 15, 20 km) with equal weight and over the five intrusion types. The chain value weights the distances by where intruders actually enter (20 % of them are 15 to 20 km from their interrogator, where detection is 88 %) and by the real mix of types (walking, the weakest, is 50 %). The three scenarios differ by at most 0.6 points (low 96.4 % [96.1, 96.8], medium 95.8 % [95.4, 96.2], high 95.9 % [95.6, 96.3], intervals overlap): the DAS hardware is the same in all three, the difference comes only from the different interrogator positions of the three equal-cost allocations, not from the drones. The optimization keeps the literature 0.969; none of these simulated values replaces it (ASSUMED coupling).

**False alarms after verification in the three scenarios (0.213 / 0.217 / 0.220 per km per day).** About 81 % of the false patrols (25.6 of 31.5 per day in medium) come from alerts routed to the site guards, `fa_site x (1 - p_site_clear)`, which do not depend on the drones; the remaining 19 % are drone- and camera-verification errors. So the three values are close for a reason, not because the scenarios share the same chain: they are NOT identical (12,190 / 12,428 / 12,614 false patrols over 394 days). In Stage 8 the scenarios did NOT use common random numbers (the streams diverged after day 1), and the equal 0.218 was a coincidence. **Stage 9 uses common random numbers** (day d of every case has the same generator streams, the response uses a fixed block of numbers per event): the intruder times are identical in the three scenarios and the non-intrusion events are identical in 394 of 394 days. The alarms still differ slightly per day (correlation 0.975) because the interrogator positions differ between the allocations, which changes the detection of the far-end events.

**Group intrusions (p_group 25 % / 50 % of the intrusion events, groups of 2 to 5 people on foot 1 to 2 m apart, ASSUMED), medium.** The number of events is the same (10,004), so verification and drone use are unchanged: verified within T_resp 37.4 % / 37.6 % against 37.1 %, false alarms unchanged. What changes is the people and the patrols: 16,089 / 22,547 persons instead of 10,004; a group needs one patrol per 2 persons (ASSUMED), the response is complete when the last patrol is on scene, so the median alarm-to-patrol time rises from 684 s to 751 s / 831 s and the 90th percentile from 1,405 s to 1,530 s / 1,612 s (patrols were never short: every confirmed event was fully staffed with 15 patrols). **Re-identification is where groups hurt:** the accuracy of the person-level links made falls from 99.9 % to 98.0 % / 95.2 %, the share of persons that get a person-level link from 95.0 % to 50.3 % / 29.3 %, the group-level accuracy from 94.9 % to 59.3 % / 42.6 %, and the wrong person-level links rise from 0.07 to 0.98 / 1.40 per 100 persons (SIMULATED lookups of `results/reid/group_events.csv`). With the drone camera error (2.5 m) larger than the 1 to 2 m spacing of the group, the camera cannot see the group structure, so even the group-level link is mostly not made.

## Number of interrogators N versus d* (`results/siting/d_star.json`, analytic; L = 145.47 km)
N = ceil(145.47 / (2 d*)). N = 5 for every d* between 14.55 km (= L / 10) and 18.18 km (= L / 8, excluded); the number is therefore constant over that range, and the uncertainty of d* (a few km) does not change it as long as d* stays inside it. Outside the range: d* < 14.55 km gives N >= 6 (d* 12.1-14.5 km: 6; 10.4-12.1 km: 7; 9.1-10.4 km: 8; 8.1-9.1 km: 9; 7.3-8.1 km: 10); d* >= 18.18 km gives N = 4 (that is the old main-model number).
| d* [km] | 7.3-8.1 | 8.1-9.1 | 9.1-10.4 | 10.4-12.1 | 12.1-14.55 | 14.55-18.18 | 18.18-24.2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| N | 10 | 9 | 8 | 7 | 6 | 5 | 4 |

## d* result (dense run, rule fixed beforehand; `results/siting/d_star.json`, `pd_curve.png`, `dstar_rule_table.csv`)
Rule (table row `siting_dstar_rule`, applied to the **type-mix Pd**, i.e. the average of the five intrusion types weighted as in Stage 9): d* = farthest distance with the LOWER 95 % limit of the monotone Pd(d) >= Pd_DAS = 0.969. Result: **d* = 14.75 km** (resolution 0.25 km; lower limit 0.9735 at 14.75 km, 0.9669 at 15 km). For comparison only: weakest-type rule 13 km (walking), point-estimate rule 15 km, upper-limit rule 17 km, first coarse run 17 km. FEBUS range option: 20 km. **N = ceil(145.47 / 29.5) = 5**, inside the 14.55-18.18 km interval where N = 5; N would become 6 if d* fell below 14.55 km (the weakest-type rule, 13 km, would give 6). The margin to the 14.55 km edge is only 0.2 km.

## Siting result at d* = 14.75 km: analytic minimum 5, actual solution 6 (`results/siting/n5_test.json`, `scripts/siting_n5_test.m`, `results/siting/sensitivity.csv`)
**The analytic minimum is N_min = 5 (ceil(145.47 / 29.5)), the actual solution is N = 6 because of the siting constraints.** Evidence (medium scenario, same candidates and objectives):
* Ideal sites (any position on the boundary, no lead-in): the minimum cover is 5 sites. With the 131 real candidates (road sites 50-200 m inside the boundary + the 5 checkpoints, lead-in fibre subtracted from the reach): the minimum cover is 6 sites. The slack of N = 5 is only 14.75 - 14.55 = 0.2 km per side.
* MILP with N = 5 forced (`Siting.Nfix`): it is feasible only because the coverage of the boundary is a violation to be minimised in stage 1, not a hard constraint: it leaves 4 cells (4.10 km of fibre: arc 23.1-23.7, 52.3-54.4 and 110.4-111.9 km of the boundary) WITHOUT DAS, with C_total 11,775,758 SAR. Each of those stretches is reachable by some candidate, but no choice of 5 allowed sites covers them all: the 5 sites would have to be placed so exactly that the allowed (road / checkpoint) positions and their lead-in fibre do not permit it.
* The lexicographic MILP minimises the number of violating cells first, so it takes N = 6: full coverage, C_total 12,654,986 SAR, i.e. **+879,228 SAR (+7.5 %) for the 4.10 km that the 5-site solution leaves uncovered**.
* Sensitivities (road 100 / 200 / 500 m, slope 5 / 10 / 15 %, waterway 25 / 50 / 100 m, inside distance 200 / 500 m): N = 6 in all 8 cases; cost 12,654,814-12,655,748 SAR; five of the six sites are the same in every case (4 checkpoints Al-Sharaye, Al-Hada, Al-Shumaisi (new), Al-Nawariyah and one road site near 58.4 km); only the road site near 108.9 km moves (97.4 km with slope 5 %, 97.9 km with road 500 m).
* The site at 86 km (Al-Shumaisi (new) checkpoint) has a ground slope of 15.3 %: it is allowed because the entrance checkpoints are exempt from the filters (table row `siting_checkpoint_exempt`; they already have buildings and infrastructure).

## Siting: three scenarios, robustness to the d* rule, cost comparison (`results/alloc_*_22_siting*.mat`, `results/siting/siting_*`)
* **Low, medium and high give the same result** at d* = 14.75 km: N = 6, C_total 12,654,986 SAR, the same six sites (boundary arcs 8.70, 29.58, 58.44, 85.95, 108.90, 125.19 km; four checkpoints Al-Sharaye, Al-Hada, Al-Shumaisi (new), Al-Nawariyah and two road sites), no unserved run, maximum optical distance 14.23 km. The scenarios differ only in the drones, which do not enter the siting.
* **Robustness to the d* rule: N = 6 under the Pd rule of the type mix (d* = 14.75 km), N = 7 under the weakest-type rule (d* = 13 km, walking): C_total 13,303,473 SAR (+648,487 SAR), sites at 1.80, 22.44, 46.24, 64.90, 85.95, 108.90, 125.19 km, maximum optical distance 11.47 km.** The analytic N_min is 6 for d* = 13 km (ceil(145.47 / 26)).
* **Cost: main model (4 interrogators) versus siting model (6 interrogators)**

| Item | Main model (4 interrogators) | Siting model (6) | Difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Interrogators (636,000 each) | 2,544,000 | 3,816,000 | +1,272,000 |
| Shelters (C_shelter = 0 in the table) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Sensing fibre (145.46 km) | 8,829,500 | 8,829,500 | 0 |
| Lead-in fibre (route factor 1.4) | not modelled | 9,480 | +9,480 |
| **C_total** | **11,373,506** | **12,654,986** | **+1,281,480 (+11.3 %)** |
| Power: interrogators + shelter cooling | 680 + 680 = 1,360 W | 1,020 + 1,020 = 2,040 W | +680 W |

The model has no operating cost in SAR, only the power draw (within the P0 budget in both). Drones (12 in the medium scenario) are the same in both models and are not part of C_total.
